thread:
liam: hey team, day 1 question. I created a hosted API key and am testing streaming but keep getting 429s intermittently. I thought hosted keys had more quota than sandbox?
devbot: welcome liam! :wave: Sandbox keys have very limited dev quotas. Hosted keys are tied to org quotas but still subject to per-user and per-route rate limits. The 429 payload should include a `Retry-After` seconds value.
liam: the responses sometimes include Retry-After and sometimes not. is that normal?
rachel: sort of. if you hit a token-rate limit you'll usually see Retry-After. if it's concurrency-related we sometimes return an immediate 429 without a header to avoid leaking capacity details. best practice: always backoff.
liam: any sample backoff logic to use?
omar: exponential backoff w/ jitter is what we use across SDKs. simple pattern: wait = min(500ms * 2^attempt + rand(0,300ms), 5000ms). respect Retry-After when present.
liam: good. I'm also seeing 429s when running embeddings with batch=24. Is batch size the culprit?
rachel: embeddings are limited by concurrency and payload size. sandbox is stricter. for sandbox keep batches <= 16 vectors and paginate if needed. hosted can handle larger batches but if many clients do batches concurrently you'll hit request-rate limits.
liam: is there a CLI to check my personal sandbox quota quickly?
devbot: internal command exists: `rwctl quota show --user liam@example.com`. if that errors, your user might not be mapped to the org yet.
liam: ran it, got "user not found". who maps accounts?
omar: infra maps GitHub/email to org. file a ticket at https://redwood.internal/it-requests with subject "map user for metrics" and tag @infra. include your github handle and demo dates if you need temporary bump.
liam: if I need a temporary sandbox bump for a demo next week, what's the SLA?
rachel: onboarding bumps are quick: fill the sandbox-increase form (pinned in #new-hires) and mention the demo time; usually 6-12h. hosted quota increases go through growth/billing and take 24-48h.
liam: nice. last Q: in code, should I try to detect 429s and switch models automatically?
omar: yes, smart fallback is common. our client pattern: on 429 try lower-concurrency/quantized variant or lower `max_tokens`, then retry with backoff. also add circuit-breaker for repeated 429s to avoid thrashing.
liam: awesome, thanks y'all. saved notes.
devbot: checklist: create infra ticket, attach github handle, request sandbox bump if demo. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
